column1: # PART 4: THE SCOPE AND DOCTRINE ASSESSMENT
# RECON03's own ACT, section 1.1, says: "An ordinary non-ACT
# receipt/checkpoint commit is not automatically disallowed, but its
# authorization and effect must be established from doctrine."
# The effect is established and it is benign: the change REMOVED a
# self-referential digest from the frozen contract and PUBLISHED it in a
# separate file. Under AGENTS.md's "No SHA-of-self claims" rule, a file
# cannot carry its own digest; the previous in-file value was
# necessarily stale. The commit therefore made the frozen contract
# self-consistent and did not change any substantive frozen content.
# The one consequence THIS ACT must record honestly is that the
# predecessor's own FROZEN CONTRACT FILE was edited AFTER the
# predecessor's CLOSE. This is an F14 observation about the
# predecessor, not a defect in the contract's substance. It is
# recorded, it is not endorsed retroactively as an ACT-authorized
# mutation, and it is NOT a reason to halt THIS ACT, because:
#   (a) the substantive frozen content is byte-identical;
#   (b) the digest THIS ACT binds to (77e2a0d5...) is the digest of the
#       contract's CURRENT committed bytes, and THIS ACT re-derives it
#       independently from the Git object;
#   (c) no production source and no other ACT's evidence was touched.
